newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid stocks push higher, strength in BBV.
newsitem.headline: Madrid stocks push higher, strength in BBV.

text.p: Madrid stocks were higher at midday on Wednesday, with strength in BBV and bourse debutante Baron de Ley bolstering the market, dealers said.
Stocks have followed the tone set by other European markets, they added, although Ibex gains are seen capped at 7,200.
The general index added 5.33 points, 0.86 percent, to 625.12 and the Ibex-35 rose 62.36 points, 0.88 percent, to 7,126.48.
BBV was up strongly, adding 210 pesetas to 13,150 in a movement one trader said was a "flight to quality after worse than expected results at Popular and Bankinter."
Popular recouped some of Tuesday's losses, adding 10 pesetas ot 36,000, while Bankinter was flat at 26,600 pesetas.
BBV, which releases results at the end of the month, is seen posting first half earnings growth of 25.7 percent, according to a Reuters poll.

Baron de Ley, a winery whose shares started trade for the first time today, was at 2,915 pesetas versus its share offering price of 2,350 pesetas. Volume was heavy, with over 1.6 million shares changing hands.
